prompt: In Ey = E-nought sin(kx minus omega t), the wave number is k = 2 pi over {{1}} and the angular frequency is omega = 2 pi f.
explanation: Lambda, the wavelength. Both symbols carry the same 2 pi: k packs 2 pi into one wavelength of SPACE, omega packs 2 pi into one period of TIME. Ey and Bz share the identical sin(kx minus omega t), which is why the two fields peak together and vanish together.

prompt: In the plane wave Ey = E-nought sin(kx minus omega t) and Bz = B-nought sin(kx minus omega t), the electric field points along y, the magnetic field along z, and the wave travels along x.
explanation: True, and the three directions are mutually perpendicular by construction. The subscript on each field names its own direction, and the x inside the bracket names the direction of travel. Hold your thumb, first finger and second finger at right angles: E, B and the direction of travel, never two of them along the same line.

why.true: Correct. The subscripts give E and B their directions, and x inside the sine gives the direction of travel.
why.false: Wrong. Read the subscripts: Ey along y, Bz along z, and the phase depends on x.

prompt: The intensity of an electromagnetic wave, I = one half epsilon-nought c E-nought squared, is measured in watts per square {{1}}.
explanation: Watts per square metre: power spread over area. The half is there because the field oscillates, so the AVERAGE of the squared sine over a cycle is one half, not one. The same one half turns up in one half C V squared and one half L I squared, always for the same reason.

prompt: Doubling the peak electric field of a wave doubles its intensity.
explanation: It QUADRUPLES it. I = one half epsilon-nought c E-nought squared, and the field is squared, so twice the field gives four times the intensity. That is why a lamp twice as bright does not feel twice as fierce, and why halving the field cuts the power to a quarter.

why.true: Wrong. The intensity depends on E-nought SQUARED, not on E-nought.
why.false: Correct. Twice the field, four times the intensity.

prompt: The Poynting vector S = one over mu-nought, times E cross B, gives the rate at which {{1}} is transported per unit area by the wave.
explanation: Energy. The name is a happy accident: the vector POINTS the way the energy travels, which is the direction of E cross B, at right angles to both fields. Its size is the power crossing each square metre, and averaging it over a cycle is exactly what gives the intensity I.
